Hi Sana —

Appreciate the clear ask and the table. Quick responses:

- Baseline uptime: our standard hosted SLA is 99.5% for the self-serve tier; for customers committing to the pilot (3-month reserved capacity with monitoring hooks) we can offer a provisional 99.9% p95 latency SLA for the region you care about, provided we agree on the traffic profile and a small committed capacity buffer. I can include a clause that requires a capacity ramp plan (mutual action plan) to lock in 99.9.

- Monthly remedy: we generally use a credit table with a monthly cap equal to 100% of the monthly bill for hosted customers. We can support an escrow-style application (credits retained and applied to future invoices) for pilots with procurement sign-off. There are two practical items: (a) definition of incident windows and what counts as maintenance; (b) whether credits are prorated per route/model.

I'll attach a suggested SLA redline and a proposed remedy table. Laura, Markus — could you scan and confirm legal/finance constraints?

Proposed next step: 30 minute sync on Monday 09:00 PT to walk the redline and the capacity ramp language.

—Jonas

Jonas/Sana —

Quick legal notes before Monday's call:

- We can offer a 99.9% uptime commitment for an agreed pilot but need explicit language carving out scheduled maintenance (we recommend a 4 hour monthly maintenance window per region, with at least 72 hours notice).

- Remedy cap: our standard cap is 100% of monthly fees; for pilot customers we are open to a fixed cap at 75% of monthly fees, but that requires a business justification (e.g., committed capacity/term). If Rivet can commit to the 3-month reserved buffer and provide telemetry hooks (API keys, trace sampling), we can reduce legal friction.

- Escrow mechanics: we can support credits rolling forward for up to six months. Beyond that, credits convert to invoice offsets rather than cash payouts. We'll add a short paragraph in Section 6 describing the escrow treatment.

Markus — can you confirm any finance-side limits on escrow duration?

Regards,

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA baseline + monthly remedy workflow for pilot

Laura/Team —

Finance check: from our side we prefer a single monthly cap and a short escrow window to keep ledger clean. Two recommendations:

1) Cap at 75% of monthly invoice for pilots under 3-month commitments, with the option to increase to 100% on renewal or if Rivet increases committed capacity by >=25%.

2) Credits may roll forward up to three billing cycles (three months). After three months, leftover credits are applied to the next invoice and cannot be cashed out. This reduces outstanding receivables and accounting complexity.

If Rivet needs a longer runway for credits, we can structure a separate credit escrow agreement, but that adds procurement lead time.

Also flag: latency SLA language should include p50/p95 windows, not just p95. Suggest p50 target of 120ms and p95 target aligned to 99.9% uptime objective — operationally helpful.

-Markus
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Sana Patel <sana@rivet.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA baseline + monthly remedy workflow for pilot — agreed edits and next steps

Sana —

Thanks for the patience. Summary of agreed positions from our internal review and proposed contract wording:

- Uptime: Redwood will commit to a provisional 99.9% regional uptime for the pilot (p95 latency target included) conditional on the mutual action plan: 3-month pilot, committed capacity buffer of 25% above expected QPS, and access to application telemetry for joint troubleshooting.

- Latency targets: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 420ms for production traffic within the agreed region. We'll include a clause that latency objectives are measured at our edge egress points and exclude third-party network transit.

- Remedy table (monthly):
  • 99.9% — no credit
  • 99.0% - 99.899% — 20% of monthly fee
  • 98.0% - 98.999% — 50% of monthly fee
  • <98.0% — 75% of monthly fee (pilot cap)

- Cap and escrow: For the pilot the monthly credit cap will be 75% of the monthly fee. Credits may be carried forward for up to three billing cycles then applied to the next invoice. Separate escrow agreements are available but would add procurement time.

- Maintenance carveouts: scheduled maintenance (<=4 hours/month per region) with 72-hour notice is excluded from uptime calculations. Emergency maintenance will be counted unless we issue a customer advisory and remediation plan.

Next steps: I attached a redlined SLA (redline-sla-template.docx) and a consolidated monthly-remedy-table.xlsx. If this matches Rivet's expectations, can you confirm by EOD Monday so your procurement team can issue the PO? If you prefer, we can get DocuSign in motion after a short call to finalize the mutual action plan.

Best,
